newsitem.title: UK: Thames Water to repair leaky pipes free - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thames Water to repair leaky pipes free - paper.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Thames Water Plc is to offer to repair leaks to its customers' supply pipes free of charge, Monday's Independent said.
The newspaper said the move is to forestall criticism of the company's high leakage rates and comes ahead of a drought summit expected to be called by the new Labour government next week.

Figures from industry regulator Ofwat show that Thames Water loses 38 percent of the treated water it puts into the mains -- more than any other company. Thames puts this down to London clay, which can fracture pipes when it shrinks during dry spells.
The newspaper said that Thames, which serves more than seven million people in and around London, will announce within three weeks its plan to repair any leakage in supply pipes.
Despite the recent wet spell, much of the south and east of England is still in drought after two dry years and a very dry start to this year.
